text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- National Library head Ivi Eenmaa is expected to get enough support from city council to become mayor of Tallinn.
- Estonian defense minister Andres Oovel signed a memorandum with French company SAGEM SA to improve Estonia's automatic fingerprint checking system.

- Thieves broke into the Narva police station and stole 50,000 kroons. The theft was discovered only moments before the director of the police department arrived together with the new prefect of Narva.
- President Lennart Meri is dissatisfied with Helmut Kohl and Germany's position on European Union and Nato expansion, the German journals Der Spiegel and Focus reported.
- Estonia will continue membership negotiations with the World Trade Organisation on May 12-18 in Geneva, the leader of the Estonian delegation Priit Kolbre said.
- The Editor-in-chief and part of the staff of the cultural weekly Kultuurileht resigned yesterday after a disagreement with the owners over money.
- The Estonian Central Union of Industry and Employers elected Ants Pilving, managing director of the plant Dvigatel, as its new leader on Tuesday.
- The opposition in the Tallinn city council is planning to luanch a no-confidence motion against deputy mayor Kalev Kallo for incompetence, Rein Voog of the Reform Party said.
- Estonia's leading commercial banks are revising their 1997 profit forecasts in the wake of better than expected results for the first four months of the year.
